papers.title: Firing Without Wiring: How REM-like Sleep Reactivation Rebalances Excitation and Inhibition to Orthogonalize Memories
papers.summary: Using recurrent neural networks trained with Equilibrium Propagation, the study shows that REM-like sleep reduces memory interference by decorrelating task-specific neuronal populations through a mechanism termed reactivation-targeted pruning, where plasticity is confined to the most recently activated population and depressive excitatory input from older-memory populations. This mechanism held under Dale's law and required only excitatory synaptic depression, without inhibitory plasticity.

papers.title: Wild ginseng adventitious roots restore sleep homeostasis in sleep-deprived Drosophila melanogaster.
papers.summary: In sleep-deprived Drosophila melanogaster, treatment with wild ginseng adventitious roots (ADV) increased total sleep duration and deep sleep while reducing sleep latency and fragmentation without inducing addiction-like behaviors. Transcriptomic analysis implicated stress-response pathways (e.g., Hsp genes), and ginsenosides Rc and F2 were identified as principal active metabolites.

papers.title: Slow-wave sleep selectively amplifies network signatures of the presumed epileptogenic zone in focal epilepsy.
papers.summary: In 22 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy undergoing intracranial EEG, NREM3 sleep selectively amplified gamma-band synchrony within the presumed epileptogenic zone (pEZ) and increased pEZ local efficiency and betweenness centrality in beta1 and gamma bands compared to wakefulness. A three-feature classifier using NREM3 aperiodic exponent, beta2 connectivity, and gamma local efficiency localized the pEZ with median AUC 0.859.

papers.title: Molecular clockwork hypothesis for the KaiABC circadian oscillations.
papers.summary: Developed a theoretical model testing the molecular clockwork hypothesis for KaiABC circadian oscillations, relating the oscillation period to KaiC ATPase activity. The model explains period changes induced by amino acid substitutions near the CI-CII domain boundary and addresses the physical basis of temperature compensation.

papers.title: Longitudinal changes in resting-state EEG eyes-closed/open delta differentiation during an Antarctic expedition.
papers.summary: In 16 Antarctic expeditioners, longitudinal resting-state EEG showed progressively negative shifts in the eyes-closed minus eyes-open delta power difference across parietal, frontal, whole-brain, and occipital regions over the expedition, most pronounced during and after the polar night. Secondary mild variations were observed in aperiodic spectral metrics, occipital sample entropy, and global delta connectivity, while microstates showed no significant changes.

papers.title: Selection on PER2 Phosphorylation Regulation Underlies Atypical Mammalian Circadian Rhythms.
papers.summary: Molecular evolution analysis of 20 PER2-associated genes across 71 mammals identified positive selection in CDK5, CSNK1E, and GSK3B, which regulate PER2 phosphorylation, in lineages with atypical circadian phenotypes. In vitro, dolphin CSNK1E increased phosphorylation at PER2 S662 and extended PER2 half-life, and zebrafish overexpressing dolphin CSNK1E showed elevated locomotor activity and reduced sleep duration.

papers.title: Is cardiovascular autonomic control during the day-to-night transition dependent on dim light melatonin onset? An exploratory analysis in healthy adults.
papers.summary: Exploratory study in 10 healthy adults using an ultra-short semi-constant routine tested whether dim-light melatonin onset (DLMO) aligns with the day-to-night transition in cardiovascular autonomic control. Cardiovascular onset times did not differ significantly from DLMO, but DLMO–CV onset differences correlated strongly with phase angle of entrainment (r > 0.75), suggesting alignment depends on entrainment phase.

papers.title: Neuroelectrophysiological correlates of extended cessation of consciousness in advanced meditators: A multimodal EEG and MEG study
papers.summary: First electrophysiological study of 'extended cessation' meditation, with five advanced meditators undergoing concurrent EEG and MEG. Extended cessation significantly increased high-frequency global coherence in all five participants without consistent effects on Lempel-Ziv complexity or power, suggesting a neural signature distinct from deep sleep and anesthesia.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomics and metabolomics reveal Cry1-associated hepatic alterations and plasma essential fatty acids as biomarkers of residual circadian disruption post-sepsis.
papers.summary: Integrated liver transcriptomics and plasma metabolomics in male mice 7 days after non-lethal LPS-induced sepsis, identifying sampling-time-independent linoleic acid and alpha-linolenic acid as candidate biomarkers of residual circadian disruption and proposing a Cry1-essential fatty acid axis. Exogenous supplementation of these fatty acids shortened rhythm re-entrainment period in male mice.

papers.title: Emerging evidence suggests that circadian disruption and muscle wasting form a self-reinforcing loop.
papers.summary: Proposes a bidirectional self-reinforcing loop in which circadian disruption and skeletal muscle wasting amplify each other, with the forward arm supported by genetic evidence (e.g., global Bmal1 knockout) and human sleep-deprivation studies and the reverse arm by correlative clinical and disease-model evidence. Argues chronotherapeutic interventions targeting this loop show preclinical efficacy and warrant clinical translation.

papers.title: Cognitive tests of pattern separation as sleep-sensitive measures in middle-aged and older adults: An exploratory study
papers.summary: Exploratory study of 34 adults aged 50+ using 7-day wrist actigraphy and sleep diaries to test whether pattern separation cognitive tasks are sensitive to objective sleep. Objective sleep quantity significantly correlated with and predicted Mnemonic Similarity Task performance when controlling for age, sex, and education.

papers.title: Astrocyte molecular rhythm disruption in nucleus accumbens promotes increased binge-like drinking in mice.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Used AAV8-Gfap-Cre to ablate molecular rhythms in nucleus accumbens astrocytes of BMAL1-floxed mice, finding increased binge-like drinking in drinking-in-the-light and drinking-in-the-dark paradigms (d = 1.44) without changes in other drinking paradigms or behaviors. Identifies a role for NAc astrocyte rhythmicity in temporal organization of reward circuitry and binge-drinking susceptibility.

papers.title: Circadian rhythms and sleep disturbances: a conceptual perspective with implications for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
papers.summary: Conceptual review of how circadian rhythm and sleep disturbances may influence autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease progression, linking circadian disruption to sympathetic activation, RAAS dysregulation, elevated vasopressin, mTOR activation, and impaired fatty acid oxidation. Discusses chronotherapy and sleep hygiene interventions, including timed antihypertensives, diuretics, tolvaptan, melatonin, and light exposure, as adjunctive strategies.

papers.title: A Humanized Mouse Model of DRPLA Recapitulates Epilepsy and Demonstrates Antisense Oligonucleotide-Mediated Disease Modification
papers.summary: Characterized a fully humanized ATN1 mouse model expressing mutant atrophin-1 with 112 CAG repeats, showing increased seizure susceptibility, spontaneous behavioral seizures on video-EEG, ataxia, and early death. Antisense oligonucleotide treatment normalized seizure threshold, reduced ataxia, protected against early death, and eliminated spontaneous seizures, supporting ATN1 as an epilepsy-related risk factor.

papers.title: Feasibility of unattended in-home polysomnography in trauma-exposed Veterans with chronic nightmares.
papers.journal: Dreaming : journal of the Association for the Study of Dreams
papers.summary: Unattended in-home polysomnography was assessed in 47 trauma-exposed U.S. Veterans with chronic nightmares: 41 (87.2%) scheduled studies were completed, but only 24 (58.5%) met all pre-specified success criteria and 29 (71%) had at least 4 hours of interpretable EEG; self-reported sleep quality was worse on the hPSG night than on a non-hPSG night.

papers.title: De-escalating Therapy in Obstructive Sleep Apnoea After Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist-Induced Weight Loss: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on weight change and OSA severity, incretin (GLP-1 and dual agonist) efficacy in OSA, and PAP withdrawal studies, noting consistent AHI, weight, and blood pressure reductions but unresolved questions about weight mediation, cardiovascular risk reduction, and true remission, and proposes a structured reversible framework for therapy de-escalation.

papers.title: Pharmacological inhibition of REV-ERBα ameliorates motor deficits in the 6-OHDA-lesioned mouse model of Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: In 6-OHDA-lesioned mice, Rev-erbα mRNA was elevated in substantia nigra TH-positive neurons, and local substantia nigra microinjection of the REV-ERBα antagonist SR8278 partially recovered motor performance and fine motor function without restoring TH expression or tissue dopamine, while enhancing striatal extracellular dopamine turnover.

papers.title: The impact of creatine on brain functions.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence that creatine supplementation can raise brain creatine and may benefit cognition under high metabolic demand (e.g., stress, sleep deprivation) and augment mood disorder treatment, possibly via mTORC1, while evidence on generalized fatigue remains ambiguous and findings are limited by methodological heterogeneity.

papers.title: TCANet: a temporal convolutional attention network for EEG-based cognitive load assessment in simulated flight tasks.
papers.summary: The authors propose TCANet, a temporal convolutional attention network using multi-branch temporal and dilated convolutions with attention to classify EEG-based cognitive load in simulated flight tasks, achieving average accuracies of 90.15% on the turning task (n=15) and 81.52% on the landing task (n=5), with task-related Theta and Alpha band differences.

papers.title: Digital behavior therapy for insomnia in the general population: secondary analysis of the multi-arm RESiLIENT trial with active comparators.
papers.summary: In a secondary analysis of the multi-arm RESiLIENT randomized controlled trial, a smartphone-delivered behavior therapy for insomnia (BI) reduced insomnia severity more than a health-information comparator (ES -0.43) and a mood-focused behavioral activation module (ES -0.26) at week 6, with effects persisting at week 26; adding BA to BI provided no additional benefit.

papers.title: A sliding window and Fourier decomposition method based 1D-CNN framework for motor imagery EEG classification.
papers.summary: The authors developed a 1D-CNN framework combining sliding window augmentation and Fourier decomposition method (FDM) for motor imagery EEG classification, achieving 93.67% accuracy on BCIC III IVa and 79.14% on BCIC IV 2a under subject-dependent evaluation, with real-time deployment on NVIDIA Jetson Nano.

papers.title: A novel age-based physiological definition of adherence to pediatric long-term non-invasive ventilation: an exploratory study.
papers.summary: This retrospective cross-sectional study proposed a novel age-based physiological definition of adherence to pediatric long-term non-invasive ventilation (≥70% of age-specific minimum recommended sleep duration on ≥70% of nights) and found it yielded lower adherence rates (66.25%) than adult-derived definitions (78.75% and 83.75%), suggesting adult thresholds overestimate adherence in children.

papers.title: The effects of multiregional fascial mobilization on heart rate and physiological parameters in patients with obstructive sleep apnea: A randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: In this randomized controlled trial of 95 men with polysomnography-confirmed moderate-to-severe OSA, a standardized 16-minute multiregional fascial mobilization protocol versus quiet supine rest produced no significant group × time interaction for heart rate after baseline adjustment (P = .476) or for systolic/diastolic blood pressure and peripheral oxygen saturation, demonstrating no specific acute effect on the assessed physiological parameters.

papers.title: Effects of West Nile Virus on behavioral and cognitive performance, circadian body temperatures, cortical Aβ and p-tau pathology, and immune measures in human apoE and human amyloid precursor protein NL-G-F/human apoE mice.
papers.summary: In middle-aged mice expressing human apoE isoforms and human amyloid precursor protein with NL-G-F mutations, West Nile virus (Kunjin strain) exposure produced apoE isoform-dependent effects on behavior, circadian body temperature, cortical p-tau levels, and immune transcripts, with soluble p-tau increased and insoluble p-tau decreased, consistent with potential antiviral roles of Aβ and p-tau.

papers.title: Biological age in the meta omics era: Integrating physical activity, sleep, and diet to reshape paths of healthy ageing.
papers.summary: This review discusses biological age as a translational endpoint linking physical activity, sleep, and diet to multi-omics changes and clinical outcomes, arguing that integrating multiple aging clocks with inflammatory, metabolic, and oxidative pathways can support reproducible strategies to slow aging and extend healthspan.

papers.title: A Reproducible Safety Assessment Model for Concurrent Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation with Implanted Intracranial Electroencephalography Electrodes.
papers.summary: Developed and validated a reproducible agarose-phantom framework for assessing TMS safety with implanted sEEG electrodes, quantifying displacement, heating, and induced currents. Across single-pulse, repetitive (1-50 Hz), and theta-burst TMS, sEEG lead displacement stayed micrometer-scale (max 1-s mean 16.27 μm), temperature increases remained within the 2°C threshold (max 0.073°C), and induced voltages and charge densities stayed below safety limits.

papers.title: Electroencephalography Changes in Emotional Recognition: A Signal Processing Approach Using Wavelet Features.
papers.summary: Analyzed EEG responses to image, video, and music emotional stimuli in 48 healthy participants using discrete wavelet transform features within an arousal-valence framework. Found left-right hemispheric differences across emotional states (p<.05), with video and music evoking stronger, more discriminable responses than images and negative emotions showing greater discriminability.

papers.title: Multiscale neural signatures of long-lag repetition learning: a simultaneous fNIRS-EEG study.
papers.summary: Used simultaneous fNIRS-EEG with a multimodal decoding framework to characterize long-lag repetition learning during a semantic judgment task in 30 participants. Repeated words reduced response times and produced a frontal N400-range repetition negativity and attenuated alpha-beta suppression, with multimodal classifiers outperforming unimodal ones.

papers.title: Beyond a Single Hypoxic Burden Value: Hypoxic Burden Ratio Assessed by Peripheral Arterial Tonometry in Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
papers.summary: Retrospectively analyzed 2136 OSA adults using peripheral arterial tonometry to compare two hypoxic burden measures, defining three operational groups based on HB_baseline versus HB_<90%. Types 2 and 3 had similar pAHI3% (26.3 vs 28.8 events/h) but markedly different HB_<90% (6.0 vs 86.5 %·min/h) and median T90 (5.4% vs 63.6%), suggesting a ratio-based framework reveals distinct hypoxemic profiles.

papers.title: Differential Cerebral Perfusion Patterns Across Migraine Phenotypes: An Exploratory ASL MRI Study.
papers.summary: Characterized cerebral blood flow alterations across migraine phenotypes using 3D pseudo-continuous ASL MRI in 143 migraine patients and 49 controls. Migraine with aura showed increased nCBF in a right cerebellar-occipitotemporal cluster (surviving covariate adjustment) versus migraine without aura, and a combined clinical-imaging model showed higher apparent AUC than clinical alone.

papers.title: Acute Psychosis and Dissociative Syndrome Following Binge Recreational Nitrous Oxide Use: A Case Report.
papers.summary: Reports a case in a female in her early 20s who developed acute psychotic and dissociative symptoms over three days after binge recreational nitrous oxide and MDMA use with sleep deprivation, with elevated homocysteine and low-normal B12 indicating functional cobalamin deficiency. Risperidone was followed by neutropenia that resolved after switching to aripiprazole, and the patient recovered by day 12 with no psychotic symptoms at three weeks.

papers.title: Pancreatic hamartoma presenting with sleep-related behavioral abnormalities due to neuroglycopenia: a case report.
papers.summary: Describes a 58-year-old woman whose paroxysmal nocturnal behavioral abnormalities, initially resembling REM sleep behavior disorder or frontal lobe epilepsy, were traced to refractory nocturnal hypoglycemia from a pancreatic tail mass. Laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy confirmed a pancreatic hamartoma composed predominantly of islet cells, after which the hypoglycemia and sleep-related behaviors resolved completely.

papers.title: Effects of multiple low-dose intranasal dexmedetomidine administration on postoperative pulmonary complications in elderly patients undergoing thoracoscopic radical resection of lung cancer: a single-center randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: A double-blind randomized controlled trial in 186 elderly patients undergoing thoracoscopic radical lung-cancer resection found that multiple low-dose intranasal dexmedetomidine reduced postoperative pulmonary complications within 7 days (9.68% vs 22.58%; RR 2.333, NNT 7.75) with a favorable safety profile. It also altered postoperative IL-6, TNF-α, and sleep questionnaire scores.

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of Integrated Chinese and Western Medicine for Depression With Anxiety and Somatic Symptoms: A Meta-Analysis.
papers.journal: International journal of psychiatry in medicine
keywords: integrated Traditional Chinese and Western medicine
papers.summary: A PRISMA-guided systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 randomized controlled trials found that integrated Traditional Chinese and Western medicine reduced depression severity (MD -3.95, 95% CI -4.71 to -3.19) and anxiety symptoms (MD -3.95, 95% CI -4.65 to -3.26) versus control interventions, with generally good tolerability but low certainty of evidence.

papers.title: Interplay of action-based prediction and top-down attention: EEG evidence for joint modulation of late perceptual processing.
papers.summary: An EEG study in which participants viewed sequential gratings that were predicted/self-generated or unpredicted/externally generated and attended or not found no modulation of early visual potentials (N1a), but P3b amplitude was reduced for predicted task-relevant stimuli and prediction-related P3b latency differences correlated with faster reaction times. Multivariate, time-frequency, and behavioral analyses suggested that top-down attention and action-based prediction jointly facilitate late perceptual and decision-related processing.

papers.title: Cannabidiol (CBD) for Pain: A Narrative Review of Evidence to Date.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesized preclinical, pharmacokinetic, and clinical evidence on cannabidiol for pain, finding strong biological plausibility but inconsistent clinical translation. High-quality trials in knee osteoarthritis, fibromyalgia, and acute low back pain failed to separate CBD from placebo, and dose-dependent hepatotoxicity risk was noted.

papers.title: Seven-day Accelerometer-derived Wrist Activity after Acute Stroke Stratified by Hemiparesis Severity: A Prospective Observational Pilot Study.
papers.summary: This prospective pilot study characterized 7-day bilateral wrist accelerometry trajectories in 24 acute stroke inpatients stratified by baseline FMA-UE severity. Severe impairment showed lower paretic activity and asymmetry at day 1, but the magnitude ratio showed no significant temporal change despite improved clinical motor scores.

papers.title: Pressure Injury Prevention in Advanced Cancer: A Narrative Review and Proposed Comfort-Prioritized, Risk-Stratified Framework.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesized evidence on pressure injury risk assessment and prevention in adults with advanced cancer and proposed a comfort-prioritized, risk-stratified framework. It notes that many preventive intervention data are extrapolated from non-oncology populations and recommends tailoring support surfaces, repositioning, dressings, and nutrition to risk, prognosis, and goals of care.

papers.title: From community diagnosis to policy dialogue: co-creating childhood obesity prevention strategies in rural and urban Portugal.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional observational study within a mixed-methods action-research framework assessed child wellbeing and co-created local childhood obesity prevention strategies across rural and urban Portuguese territories. It identified favorable quality of life and sleep but concerns regarding physical activity, screen time, psychological symptoms, school meals, and community safety.

papers.title: A comparative evaluation of thiol/disulfide homeostasis and ischemia-modified albumin levels in patients with heroin use disorder in remission and detoxification.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study compared thiol/disulfide homeostasis and ischemia-modified albumin between 52 heroin use disorder patients in remission and 49 in detoxification. Redox and ischemia markers did not differ by treatment phase but correlated with depression, craving, and health-lifestyle scores, suggesting they track symptom severity rather than detoxification status.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
